capabilities: Scan for unused, duplicate, oversized, junk-named, and misplaced attachments
Cross-check resolved links against a raw-content mention scan before flagging files unused
Bulk trash, move, and dedupe attachments with link-preserving moves and renames
Detect broken links pointing at missing attachments
Export Markdown reports and restore past trash, move, and rename actions from history
extras: Freemium: the free tier audits fully and cleans one file at a time; a one-time Pro payment (offline license key, no account) unlocks unlimited bulk cleanup, saved scan profiles, custom rules, and severity tuning. Restore is free at any size. Everything runs locally with no network calls.
motivation: The author built it because most attachment tools optimize for naming or filing, while the hard part — deciding which files can be safely moved or trashed — was left to guesswork.
problem: Obsidian offers no safe way to identify truly unused attachments, and generic orphan finders rely on resolved links alone, misclassifying files referenced in canvas, frontmatter, raw HTML, or CSS snippets.

requires.name: Attachment Audit Pro license (one-time purchase via Buy Me a Coffee)

summary: Attachment cleanup tool that audits vault attachments for orphans, duplicates, oversized files, junk names, and misplaced files, with evidence before deletion.
